newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: QNI says institutions warm to Gencor deal.
newsitem.headline: QNI says institutions warm to Gencor deal.

text.p: Nickel and cobalt producer QNI Ltd said on Tuesday local institutional shareholders had indicated they were reacting favourably to a revised A$2.3 billion merger deal with the nickel arm of South African resources group Gencor Ltd.

"Yes, we've had so far today an indication from a major institutional shareholder and it's favourable," QNI's chief financial officer, Christopher Foll, told a news briefing. "We've received quite a lot of support from Australian institutions," Foll said.

Earlier QNI announced revised terms for the merger including a reduction in the shares being issued to Gencor's base metals arm, Billiton Plc to 455.8 million (52.5 percent) from 504.03 million (55 percent) and an increase in the capital return to shareholders to 30 cents from 28 cents.
"They (the institutions) are not (not) beating a drum at our door and saying it's a lousy deal," Foll said.
Foll said it was fair to say that Australian institutions had originally viewed the merger negatively which contrasted with a more favourable perception from overseas shareholders.
An independent report from Grant Samuel & Associates said the merger deal was fair and reasonable and would transform QNI into one of the five biggest nickel producers in the world.
Foll said local insitutions were now a lot more knowledgeable about the merged group's assets, including the Cerro Matoso nickel mine in Columbia.
"They are now more comfortable with the site and its assets," Foll said.
"I think it's fair to say there's a lot more knowledge out there than there was two months ago," he said.
Foll described negotiations on the revised deal as "robust" as the two groups progressed through finalisation of both financial and other due diligence matters.
"The important thing is in the end we agreed. Both parties are convinced this is going to be an excellent outcome," he said.
"Yes, QNI shareholders have managed to attain a slightly more advantageous position than they had before," Foll said.
QNI shares were 10 cents lower at A$2.40 at 4.00 p.m. (0600 GMT).
